patent_summary: BASF SE's application discloses two crystalline forms of tembotrione, 2-[2-chloro-4-methylsulfonyl-3-(2,2,2-trifluoroethoxymethyl)benzoyl]cyclohexan-1,3-dione, designated form A and form C and each characterised by a table of X-ray powder reflections, a single-crystal unit cell and a DSC melting range, together with a process for each, crystallization from the "polar organic solvents" listed at [0013] (line 163) for form A and "crystallization from a hot solution of tembotrione in 2,2-dimethylpropanol (tert. amyl alcohol)" ([0046], line 291) or in an aromatic or aromatic-aliphatic hydrocarbon for form C, plus plant protection agents containing either form, a method of combating undesired plant growth, and a third modification which is described and excluded, [0063] (line 325) recording that "modification B cannot be stably formulated". No bond-forming or bond-breaking step is described or exemplified anywhere: [0021] (line 179) contemplates that the solution may come from "Preparation of the tembotrione by a chemical reaction" and [0040] (line 220) refers that preparation out to WO 00/21924, so every operation actually reported dissolves one molecule and crystallises it again, the recorded variables being solvent, cooling and seeding.
novelty_claims: The patent positions the solid forms themselves as new, claim 16 (line 714) requiring a form A that displays "at least 3 of the following reflections" out of nine listed and claim 20 (line 753) a form C displaying at least three of seven, with "1-15 (canceled)" (line 712) leaving claims 16 to 33 live, of which only 16 and 20 stand without reference to another claim while 19, 23, 24, 28, 32 and 33 refer back to them but claim a different statutory class and so are independent in substance; that is offered against [0003] (line 80), which says of WO 00/21924 that "This procedure yields tembotrione as an oil or as an amorphous solid". Those thresholds and the tabulated powder data discriminate all three modifications cleanly and in both directions, form A matching all nine reflections of claim 16 and form B only two, its 5.6 and its 11.2 inside 11.1±0.2, one short of the threshold because its 9.2 falls 0.1 outside the 8.9±0.2 window and its 18.5 falls 0.2 outside the 18.9±0.2 window, form C matching none of the nine, and neither A nor B matching any of claim 20's seven; what stays narrow is the low-angle coincidence, claim 16 reciting 5.6 for form A where the form A table prints "| 5.5 ± 0.2 | 15.92 ± 0.07 |" ([0010], line 97) and the form B table prints "| 5.6 ± 0.2 | 15.77 ± 0.07 |" ([0064] table, line 335), and the DSC onsets, which do not discriminate the two at all, form A "typically lies in the range from about 118° C. to 124° C" ([0012], line 161) against form B's "typically lies in the range from about 118° C. to 123° C" ([0065], line 354); the document's own numbers also fail to support the slow-against-rapid cooling distinction on which its two processes rest, since [0031] (line 199) puts form A crystallisation at "the cooling rate is preferably less than 10 K/min", under 600 K/hr, while [0056] (line 311) defines form C's rapid cooling as "at a cooling rate of 30 to 120 K/hr", 0.5 to 2 K/min, so the whole preferred form C window lies inside the preferred form A window; the same paragraph adds that "Rapid cooling is not necessary, when seed crystals of form C are used" (line 311), and Example 15, the only gram-scale run, takes that route, seeding at 101 degrees C where "some seed crystals of the form C (tip of a spatula) were added without stirring" (line 437) and then cooling slowly. What the examples do establish is that with the regime held fixed the solvent selects the form, three preparations sharing one protocol of a boiling solution sealed in a test vessel, held in an ice-water bath about 40 minutes, on an identical 150 mg charge, differing only in solvent and in the volume needed to dissolve it: "0.15 ml of boiling methanol" (Example 1, line 374) gave form A, "0.50 ml of boiling 2,2-dimethylpropanol" (Example 14, line 426) gave form C and "0.20 ml of boiling n-pentanol" (Comparative Example 1, line 443) gave form B, each identified by powder diffraction alone, no example measuring polymorph content; the converse comparison, Comparative Example 16 on the form C solvent giving "| 16 | 2,2-dimethylpropanol | small agglomerates | B + C |" (line 488), is suggestive rather than controlled, differing from Example 14 in charge, concentration, hold time and cooling, "sealed and placed in polystyrene container and left there overnight" (line 479). Against that, no yield, isolated mass or measured purity is reported for any individual preparation, the content figures being generic, "a tembotrione content of as a rule at least 90 wt. %, often 94 wt. %" ([0039], line 218) and its form C counterpart at [0062] (line 323); the asserted formulation advantage has no supporting trial; the three drawing sheets are diffractograms of forms A, B and C carrying no printed peak positions, one of them of excluded matter per [0069] (line 362); and the printed defects, recorded as printed and repaired in neither direction, are the form C cell volume "| volume | 1811.3(4) nm^3 |" (line 256) in nm cubed where cubic Angstroms are meant, the solvent missing from "a hot solution of tembotrione in is prepared" ([0048], line 295), form B made "using n-pentanol instead of 2,2-dimethylpropanol as the solvent" ([0066], line 356) although that solvent belongs to the form C process, methanol both listed as suitable at [0013] (line 163) and named among the unsuitable solvents to be removed at [0024] (line 185), the gloss of 2,2-dimethylpropanol as "tert. amyl alcohol" (line 291) naming a different compound, "75 parts by weight of form A or form B" ([0148], line 680) naming the excluded form where nine sibling recipes name form C, formulation IX summing to 101 parts ([0150], line 684), the broken chemical name in claim 16 (line 714), and the heading "Comparative Examples 21 to 22" (line 507) standing over a table that carries a third row, 23 (line 515). Nor does the document settle which of its two claimed forms is thermodynamically stable, the stability studies, run on material "suspended in a mixture of methanol with water" ([0083], line 525) under cyclic temperature, reporting that after 2 days "a mixture of forms A, B and C had converted into form A" ([0084], line 527), that after 8 days "the pure modifications A and C were unchanged" ([0085], line 529), and that after 3 days "modification B had converted completely into modification C" ([0086], line 531), so a mixture containing B goes to A while B alone goes to C, and the document never reconciles the two conversions nor ranks A against C.
